reasoning: Independently re-verified against primary source. OBJPNT (BZMTNS.MAC:485-495) enumerates objects from index 0: line 490 '.WORD EX2TBL,EX1TBL,R2D3TB,BATBL' puts BATBL at object 0x17, and line 492 '.WORD EX1TBL,EX4TBL,TLETBL,ZONTBL' puts TLETBL at 0x1E and ZONTBL at 0x1F. LOGOBJ (BZMTNS.MAC:846 'LOGOBJ:\t.BYTE 17,80,1E,80,1F,80', the finding's primary source citation, verbatim-correct) lists exactly objects 0x17/0x1E/0x1F. LOGOBJ is consumed by '.SBTTL BATTLE ZONE LOGO' / 'HANDLE LOGO DISPLAY' (BZONE.MAC:701-703), 'LDA AY,LOGOBJ ;C SET UP OBJ #,X,Y' (BZONE.MAC:739), whose kludge 'IF LOGO HIGH ENOUGH TO BRING OUT "ZONE"' (BZONE.MAC:755-756) names ZONTBL. BATBL/TLETBL/ZONTBL are also 3D object-model tables in the identical '.BYTE(size)+.MWORD(verts)' format (BZONE.MAC:4882/4903/4925), same as PYRTBL/CUBTBL; the '.MWORD ..A,..B,..C' macro (BZONE.MAC:4879) does expand to '.NWORD ..A*4,..B*4,..C*2', and decoding BATBL's verts yields z=x/8 (e.g. .MWORD 100,200,25 -> x=400,z=50), i.e. the logo recedes in depth as claimed. Mnemonics spell BAT-TLE-ZON(E). The real mountain-scape is MTNS/MTN0-7 (BZMTNS.MAC:11-183), drawn by MOUNTS (BZONE.MAC:1240-1247, mountains fetched via 'LDA AY,MTNS' at :1367); BATBL is never referenced by MOUNTS. The audit plan's ground-truth label 'BATBL = the mountain-scape table' is therefore refuted by source; this is a BOOK_WAS_WRONG correction to the plan, not a code defect. Survives.
corrections: Supporting prose mislabels the OBJPNT table's file: the finding writes '(BZONE.MAC:490: .WORD EX2TBL,EX1TBL,R2D3TB,BATBL)', but that line lives in BZMTNS.MAC:490, not BZONE.MAC:490 (BZONE.MAC:490 is 'LDA I,10. ;C INIT DIVIDER'). The OBJPNT table is defined in BZMTNS.MAC, not BZONE.MAC. The finding's primary 'source' field (BZMTNS.MAC:846 LOGOBJ) is correct and the object-index substance is unaffected.

reasoning: The clone's premise is demonstrably false. horizon.ts:6-8 asserts 'the disassembly quarry holds no horizon picture data ... zero hits for horizon/volcano/moon', and horizon.ts:53-60 builds MOUNTAIN_RIDGE as 49 samples of a fixed two-sine profile (cited line horizon.ts:57 matches verbatim). But BZMTNS.MAC:11-183 IS the mountain picture data: MTNS (BZMTNS.MAC:11) dispatches eight authored silhouette segments MTN0..MTN7 via JSRL, each a run of relative 'VCTR dx,dy,brite' strokes. Source cite BZMTNS.MAC:19 'MTN0:\tVCTR 0,40,0' is verbatim-correct. Governing radix is 16: the nearest preceding '.RADIX 16' is BZMTNS.MAC:8, and the '.RADIX 10' regions begin at line 240 -- AFTER MTN0-7 end at 183 -- so every VCTR delta is hex. MTN0 opens with dy +0x40=+64; peaks reach dy 0x60=96 (MTN6, BZMTNS.MAC:162 'VCTR 0,60,0') and dx runs of 0xA0=160 appear (e.g. :76,:82,:143). MOUNTS' 50$ routine (BZONE.MAC:1365-1372) indexes MTNS with 'AND I,0E' (8 two-byte entries), tiling the 8 chunks around the wrap by view angle. This is authored hex vector geometry, structurally unrelated to a procedural two-sine fit. Real DIVERGENCE; survives.

Verified. The clone's MOON (horizon.ts:75-89; cited line horizon.ts:81 matches) is an independently authored crescent -- an outer disc arc plus an offset inner terminator arc. The ROM moon is embedded inside the first mountain segment MTN0 (BZMTNS.MAC:36-67, delimited ';MOON' at :36 through ';END OF MOON' at :67). Source cite BZMTNS.MAC:36 '\tVCTR 5,-0C,7\t\t;MOON' is verbatim-correct; radix 16 governs (nearest '.RADIX 16' at BZMTNS.MAC:8), so 'VCTR 5,-0C,7' = dx +5, dy -0x0C(-12), brite 7. The three-tier structure holds: PART A bright disc outline at brite 7 (BZMTNS.MAC:36-49, ';END OF MOON PART A' at :49, every stroke brite 7); PART B terminator at brite 2 (BZMTNS.MAC:50-55, ';END OF MOON PART B' at :55, every stroke brite 2); inner detail run predominantly brite 5 (BZMTNS.MAC:56-67). Because the moon rides inside MTN0 it sits at a fixed azimuth on the mountain ring in both implementations, as the finding notes. The clone reproduces the crescent FORM but authors its own position/size and flattens the 3-tier brightness -- a real DIVERGENCE. Survives.
corrections: Minor precision: the finding labels the inner detail run 'brite 5 (BZMTNS.MAC:56-67)', but the pure brite-5 strokes are lines 57-66; line 56 ('VCTR 1B,3,0') is a brite-0 positioning move and line 67 ('VCTR 1,1,2') closes at brite 2. Immaterial to the divergence.

reasoning: Mechanism verified exactly. In MOUNTS, 'LDA BOUNCE ;C PROVIDE BOUNCE' (BZONE.MAC:1265, verbatim source cite) is followed by four LSRs (BZONE.MAC:1266-1269), i.e. BOUNCE>>4 = BOUNCE/16, then (when non-zero) subtracted from the mountain beam's Y low byte 'SEC / LDA XCOMP+2 / SBC TEMP1 / STA XCOMP+2' with the Y high byte forced to -1 (BZONE.MAC:1271-1277), shifting the whole mountain drawing origin downward by BOUNCE/16 vector units. BOUNCE is 'COLLISION BOUNCE VIEW AMT' (BZONE.MAC:275) driven by BOUNCE CONTROL (BZONE.MAC:2124, routine BOUND at :2132), so on obstacle collision the mountain range visibly jolts vertically. The clone's backdrop Y is purely elevation-driven -- panoramaToNdc 'y = Math.tan(elevation)/(Math.tan(H_FOV/2)/aspect)' (horizon.ts:132, verbatim) with the explicit note 'y is heading-independent -- the camera never pitches' (horizon.ts:118-119) -- and horizon.ts carries no BOUNCE plumbing at all. Real ROM effect omitted by the clone. Survives.

Both halves verified. Half 1 (clone draws a static cone, no ejecta): horizon.ts:63-72 defines VOLCANO as a fixed cone-with-crater polyline (cited line horizon.ts:66 '[0.72, 0]' matches), and horizon.ts:29-31 explicitly defers eruption animation -- so the clone draws a cone but no rocks. Half 2 (ROM has no cone, only an eruption point): MOUNTS checks whether the volcano is on-screen via TANGLE in [0x39,0x88] (BZONE.MAC:1290-1294), then 'JSR VGCNTR ;C MOVE BEAM TO TOP OF VOLCANO' (BZONE.MAC:1318, verbatim source cite) positions the beam a fixed 0x5E above the horizon at the volcano azimuth (BZONE.MAC:1312-1315) and plots the NOROCK=5 flying rocks as aging DOTs via a VGVTR2+VGDOT loop with brightness (OBJTIM<<3)&0xE0 (BZONE.MAC:1325-1364). A source-wide 'VOLC' search returns only VOLCNO rock movement (BZONE.MAC:1377-1449), the OBJTIM 'VOLCANO STUFF' storage (:320), the on-screen test (:1290), and the beam-positioning (:1318) -- NO volcano cone silhouette geometry exists anywhere. The clone inverts the ROM (cone-no-ejecta vs ejecta-no-cone). Survives.
